headline: A 2014 law directs Congress to award one Congressional Gold Medal to World War II members of the Civil Air Patrol and sets rules for displaying it and selling bronze copies.
what_it_does: The law tells the leaders of the Senate and House to arrange a single Congressional Gold Medal honoring World War II Civil Air Patrol members as a group for their military service. The medal must be displayed at the Smithsonian Institution, and Congress expresses a wish that it also be shown at places linked to the Civil Air Patrol. The Treasury Secretary may strike and sell bronze duplicates priced to cover their cost, with the money going to the United States Mint Public Enterprise Fund.
